old: Subject of nivarteta is buddhiḥ, with kṛtā, kaluṣā, caturvidhā and sthitā agreeing. na-agatvā: na negates nivarteta, agatvā = 'without having gone' (a-gatvā), so the sense is 'would not turn back without reaching the end'. kaluṣā kṛtā taken as 'made stained' (alternative: 'made, stained'). caturvidhā 'fourfold' agrees with buddhiḥ and alludes to the four upadhās. sattvavat 'possessing spirit' (sattva = spirit, glossary 5.6). ca 'and' joins the unit to what precedes.
new: Subject of nivarteta is buddhiḥ, with kṛtā, kaluṣā, caturvidhā and sthitā agreeing. na-agatvā: na negates nivarteta, agatvā = 'without having gone' (a-gatvā), so the sense is 'would not turn back without reaching the end'. kaluṣā kṛtā taken as 'made stained' (alternative: 'made, stained'). caturvidhā 'fourfold' agrees with buddhiḥ and alludes to the four upadhās. sattvavat 'possessing spirit' (sattva = spirit, glossary 5.6). ca 'and' joins the unit to what precedes. caturvidhā is nominative singular feminine, so it agrees with buddhiḥ; agreement with upadhābhiḥ would be caturvidhābhiḥ.
